body.p: Favorable reconsideration of this application is respectfully requested in view of the following remarks.

Claims 1, 10, and 14 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over U.S. Patent Application Publication No. 2004/0077093 to Pan in view of U.S. Patent Application Publication No. 2014/0276169 to Chua.
The rejections are respectfully traversed for at least the following reasons.

The Official Action relies on Pan as teaching most of the features of claim 1, except for an air inlet comprising a plurality of slits, which is considered to be derivable from Chua (see Official Action, point 2, pages 7-8).

Pan relates to an apparatus for detecting bacteria in a subject. Fig. 2 depicts a breath sampler (101), which has a tube (107) that extends between an open mouthpiece end (111) and an open intake end (113). A check valve (115) arranged near the intake end restricts flow through the tube to a direction toward the mouthpiece end and blocks flow out ofthe intake end. A sample collection branch (109) connected to a sample container (117) branches from the tube between the intake end and the mouthpiece end. A second check valve (123) is disposed in the sample collection branch. Further, the container has a vent (119) with yet another check valve (121) that permits the flow of air out of the container upon exhalation. This arrangement is structurally different than that of the breath sampler of claim 1.

To start, the Official Action has taken the check valve (115) as corresponding to the one- way outlet valve of the non-rebreather part and to the air inlet comprising a slit in a wall of the breath sampler (See Official Action, point 2, page 7, "a one-way outlet valve (115)...an air inlet comprising a slit in a wall of the breath sample ("slit," para [0063])). This is incompatible with the language of claim 1 and thus in error. Specifically, claim I recites that the non-rebreather part comprises a one-way outlet valve arranged to allow air to exit the non-rebreather part and an air inlet comprising a plurality of slits in a wall of the breath sampler. As mentioned above, Pan's check valve (115) explicitly "restricts flow through the tube at the intake end to a direction toward the mouthpiece end Ill and blocks flow out of the intake end" (Pan at para. [0063]). In this sense, check valve (115) permits air to be taken in through the intake end but does not permit air to exit the tube (non-rebreather part). Check valve (115) thus does not and cannot reasonably be considered to correspond to the recited one-way outlet valve.

Check valve (115) also cannot fully correspond with the recited air inlet since "Pan does not expressly disclose the air inlet comprising a plurality of slits," as already acknowledged by the Official Action (see Official Action, point 2, page 8). In addition to this general deficiency, it is further respectfully pointed out the claim I recites an air inlet comprising a plurality of slits in a wall of the breath sampler. Attention is respectfully drawn to the fact that the 'slit' mentioned in Pan is in the check valve (115), not in the wall of the tube (breath sampler) itself (Pan at para. [0063], which provides "check valve 115 may be of any suitable construction, such as a generally

cone-shaped diaphragm having a slit in its small end"). That the slit is not comprised in the wall of the tube (breath sampler) is further apparent from at least Fig. 3 of Pan. Compare Fig. 3 (intake end 113) of Pan with Fig. 6E (inlet 140), for example, of the present application.

Similarly, Chua, which relates to a divided nasal cannula, merely teaches another one-way valve 50; the valve generally comprises a sealed opening which is provided with at least one slit, and possibly a plurality of slits, which allows the valve to open when there is a suitable pressure differential on opposed sides of the valve (see Chua at para. [0033]). Chua suffers from the same deficiencies as Pan in that it does not teach or reasonably suggest an air inlet comprising a plurality of slits in a wall of the breath sampler. Accordingly, even if the ordinarily skilled artisan had consulted Chua if and when seeking to modify Pan's breath sampler, he/she would still not have arrived at the breath sampler of claim 1.

Turning back to Pan, the Official Action further takes "the structure that branches away from 107 via 109", i.e., the sample collection branch (109), as corresponding to the recited sample delivery part. However, this is structurally inconsistent with claim 1, which recites that the sample delivery part is in fluid communication with the non-breather part (tube 107) via the one-way outlet valve. As is clearly shown in Fig. 2 of Pan, check valve (115), which is arranged near the intake end (113) of the tube, cannot reasonably be considered to place the sample delivery part (109) branching away from (107) in fluid communication with the non-breather part (107).

Further, the Official Action takes the check valve (121) in vent (119) as corresponding to the recited return inlet in the downstream portion of the sample delivery part. This is also problematic since, like the other check valves, air is only permitted to flow in a single direction

(Pan at para. [0064], which provides that "check valve 121 in the vent 119 permits flow of air out of the container 117 upon exhalation, but when the subject is not providing air pressure, closes the container vent to the influx of ambient air and to outflow of liquid L"). Thus, check valve (121) is not a return inlet since it is not possible for air (the breath) to re-enter the sample delivery part therefrom.

In view of the foregoing structural inconsistencies between Pan and claim 1, it further logically follows, that Pan further fails to teach or render obvious the path of the breath sample therethrough; more specifically, Pan fails to teach or reasonably suggest that the breath sample passes through the non-rebreather part, is delivered via the sample delivery part to the sample outlet into the sample collection chamber, passes through the liquid capture interface in the sample collection chamber, then re-enters the sample delivery part from the sample collection chamber via the return inlet, and escapes the breath sampler via the exhaust.

For the sake of completeness, it is recognized that Dr Moschos, Nashed, Dompeling, King- Smith, Ahmad, Akouka, Eichler, Meka, Ku, Lui, Phillips, and Kline were also cited by the Official Action but solely with respect to features set forth in dependent claims. Dr Moschos, Nashed, Dompeling, King-Smith, Ahmad, Akouka, Eichler, Meka, Ku, Lui, Phillips, and Kline each lack any disclosure or reasonable suggestion of at least a non-rebreather part with a one-way outlet valve and an air inlet comprising a plurality of slits in a wall of the breath sampler. Consequently, none of Dr Moschos, Nashed, Dompeling, King-Smith, Ahmad, Akouka, Eichler, Meka, Ku, Lui, Phillips, and Kline can be applied to remedy the aforementioned deficiencies of Pan and Chua.

For at least the reasons discussed herein, it is respectfully submitted that the disclosures in Pan, Chua, Dr Moschos, Nashed, Dompeling, King-Smith, Ahmad, Akouka, Eichler, Meka, Ku, Lui, Phillips, and Kline, whether taken individually or in combination, would not have rendered the breath sampler set forth in claim 1 obvious.

The dependent claims are patentable over the cited references at least by virtue of their dependence from independent claim 1. A detailed discussion of the additional distinguishing features recited in the dependent claims is thus not set forth at this time. Applicant reserves the right to present such arguments later during prosecution or appeal.
Reconsideration and withdrawal of the rejection is respectfully requested.

Early and favorable action with respect to this application is respectfully requested. In view of the above amendments and remarks, it is respectfully submitted that all of the claims now pending in the instant application should be allowable, and reconsideration thereof is respectfully requested.

Should any questions arise in connection with this application or should the Examiner believe that a telephone conference with the undersigned would be helpful in resolving any remaining issues pertaining to this application, the undersigned respectfully requests to be contacted at the number or email indicated below.
Respectfully submitted,
